_meta.target_environment: Linux host with Docker Engine and Docker Compose v2
_meta.purpose: Define the steps a fresh Linux environment must complete before any RIFT Gate 3 experiment is run. Completing all steps with all checks passing constitutes a 'clean environment'.

host_requirements: Linux kernel 5.x+ (required for tc netem used by rift-eval NET_ADMIN cap)
Docker Engine 24+ or Docker Desktop on Linux
Docker Compose v2 (compose plugin, not standalone docker-compose)
Sufficient disk for image pulls: ~3–4 GB estimated
network_requirements: Internet access to gcr.io and hub.docker.com for image pulls
No firewall blocking outbound 443 to gcr.io

phases.name: Pull all images
phases.description: Pull all images before attempting to start containers. This separates pull failures from startup failures.

commands.purpose: Pull all non-built service images (excludes rift-eval which is built)
commands.failure_if: Any image returns 'not found' or 'manifest unknown' — indicates image tag mismatch

phases.name: Build RIFT evaluation harness image
phases.description: Build the rift-eval image from docker/Dockerfile

commands.cmd: BUILD_DATE=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) GIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) HOST_OS=$(uname -s) HOST_KERNEL=$(uname -r) docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml build rift-eval

phases.name: Start all containers
phases.description: Bring up the full stack in detached mode

commands.failure_if: Any service exits immediately (check with 'docker compose ps')

commands.purpose: Allow services time to initialize before health checks
Verify all containers are in 'running' or 'Up' state

phases.name: Service port connectivity checks
phases.description: Verify each service is accepting connections on its expected port within the Docker network, and verify host-exposed ports from outside.

commands.purpose: Verify boutique-frontend HTTP on host port 8080
commands.failure_if: Connection refused or non-200 HTTP status

commands.purpose: Verify Prometheus health on host port 9090
Verify Jaeger UI on host port 16686

commands.cmd: docker exec boutique-cart sh -c 'nc -z boutique-redis 6379 && echo redis:OK'
commands.purpose: Verify cart can reach Redis on internal network
commands.failure_if: Connection refused or nc not available in container

phases.name: Prometheus targets check
phases.description: Query Prometheus API to inspect scrape target status. Note: most boutique service targets are expected to show 'down' (see KI-003 — gRPC ports do not expose /metrics). Prometheus self-scrape and any HTTP-serving targets should be UP.

commands.cmd: curl -sf 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); up=[t['labels']['job'] for t in d['data']['activeTargets'] if t['health']=='up']; print('UP targets:', up)"
commands.purpose: List all Prometheus targets currently in UP state
commands.note: Only 'prometheus' (self-scrape) is expected UP. Boutique service scrapes will show 'down' due to KI-003.

commands.cmd: curl -sf 'http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); down=[t['labels']['job'] for t in d['data']['activeTargets'] if t['health']!='up']; print('DOWN targets:', down)"
commands.note: All boutique service jobs will appear here. This is expected and documented in KI-003.

phases.pass_criteria: Prometheus is reachable and self-scrape target 'prometheus' is UP. DOWN boutique targets are acceptable given KI-003.
phases.fail_criteria: Prometheus itself is unreachable, or the API returns an error

phases.name: Jaeger trace ingestion check
phases.description: Verify Jaeger is receiving spans. After the loadgen has been running for ~60s, at least one service should appear in Jaeger.

commands.purpose: Wait for loadgen to generate sufficient traffic for traces to appear

commands.cmd: curl -sf 'http://localhost:16686/api/services' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('Jaeger services:', d.get('data', []))"
commands.purpose: List services that have sent traces to Jaeger
commands.failure_if: Service list is empty after 60s of loadgen traffic

phases.name: Load generator activity check
phases.description: Verify boutique-loadgen is actively generating requests.

commands.purpose: Check recent loadgen log output for request activity
commands.note: Look for Locust HTTP request log lines. Absence of requests after 30s indicates loadgen startup failure (see KI-002).

phases.name: Startup error rate check
phases.description: After 2 minutes of running, inspect frontend and loadgen logs for sustained error rates. Transient errors in the first 30s are expected due to KI-002.

commands.purpose: Count error/panic/fatal lines in the last minute of frontend logs
commands.note: A count of 0 indicates a clean steady-state. Counts > 0 warrant log inspection.

commands.purpose: Count Locust failure lines in the last minute
commands.note: Transient startup failures (first 30s) are excluded by --since 1m.

clean_environment_definition.description: A 'clean environment' for RIFT Gate 3 experiments satisfies ALL of the following:
criteria: All 14 containers listed in docker-compose.yml are in state 'Up' (not 'Exit', not 'Restarting')
Prometheus is reachable and returning 200 at localhost:9090/-/healthy
Jaeger UI is reachable at localhost:16686
Jaeger API /api/services returns at least one service name after 60s of loadgen traffic
boutique-loadgen logs show active Locust HTTP request lines
No sustained error rate in boutique-frontend logs after the 30s startup window
RIFT harness (rift-eval) can reach Prometheus and Jaeger via internal network names
explicitly_acceptable_states: Prometheus targets for boutique services show 'down' (KI-003 — expected, not a gate failure)
Transient loadgen connection errors in the first 30s (KI-002 — expected, not a gate failure)

commands.purpose: Stop and remove all containers and named volumes. Run between experiments to ensure clean state.
commands.note: -v removes named volumes (rift-artifacts, prometheus-data, jaeger-data); omit -v to preserve artifacts

total_estimated_duration_seconds.note: ~10 minutes on a fast Linux host with warm Docker layer cache; ~20 minutes on first pull on slow connection
